subject_matter: Fact — the concept space of fact in philosophical discourse: what is the case, what makes true, what is instituted, what one is thrown into, what is made
source: Husserl, Logical Investigations (Sachverhalt); Wittgenstein, Tractatus 2–2.01; Russell, The Philosophy of Logical Atomism (1918); Armstrong, A World of States of Affairs (1997); Durkheim, The Rules of Sociological Method (1895); Searle, The Construction of Social Reality (1995); Heidegger, Being and Time §29 (Faktizität); Sartre, Being and Nothingness; Fleck, Genesis and Development of a Scientific Fact (1935); Latour & Woolgar, Laboratory Life (1979)

signature.meaning: X counts as Y in context C (Searle): the first is taken as the second under a constitutive rule
the first is constituted by the second (collective representation, thought collective, constitution)
the first finds itself delivered over to the second (Geworfenheit)
the first obtains independently of the second
